data.long_meaning: Inder is a name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘indra’, which refers to a deity in Hindu mythology. Indra is the king of gods, associated with rain, thunder, and the sky. He is a powerful and revered figure, often invoked for protection and prosperity. The name Inder carries the meaning “Lord, King, God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Inder usually hope their child will grow to embody lord, king, god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Inder is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Indra', which translates to 'ruler' or 'lord'. In Hindu mythology, Indra is the God of the heavens and the deity of the cosmos. He is considered the king of all gods and is responsible for rains and thunderstorms. This ancient deity continues to hold a significant place in modern Hindu spirituality, with many devotees worshipping him for protection and prosperity. In popular culture, Inder's image has been depicted in various ways, including as a powerful warrior or as a benevolent ruler. His legacy extends to various platforms, including art, literature, music, and film.
